title: First Spanish Republic
capsule: The First Spanish Republic (11 February 1873 – 29 December 1874) was proclaimed when King Amadeo I abdicated and the Cortes voted to establish a republic, Spain's first. Four presidents followed in rapid succession — Estanislao Figueras, Francisco Pi i Margall (who resigned after 37 days rather than prosecute the Cantonalist rebellion), Nicolás Salmerón, and Emilio Castelar — against a backdrop of the Carlist War in the north, a federalist cantonal uprising in the south and east (the Cantonalist revolt), and a colonial insurrection in Cuba. General Manuel Pavía dissolved the Cortes by force on 3 January 1874, handing power to a military directorate under Francisco Serrano; General Arsenio Martínez Campos then proclaimed the Bourbon restoration on 29 December 1874, bringing Alfonso XII to the throne.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is simply that of peninsular Spain plus Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines; the republic's administrative control over the Canton territories fluctuated significantly in 1873.
